143	// authed resolves the request's API key to the member it acts for, or answers 401. Viewers may only read: any other method
144	// answers 403.
145	func (s *Server) authed(h handler) http.HandlerFunc {
146		return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
147			token, ok := strings.CutPrefix(r.Header.Get("Authorization"), "Bearer ")
148			if !ok {
149				writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "send an API key as Authorization: Bearer <token>")
150				return
151			}
152			key, ok := s.store.APIKeyByToken(strings.TrimSpace(token))
153			if !ok || key.RevokedAt != nil {
154				writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "unknown or revoked API key")
155				return
156			}
157			m, ok := s.store.Member(key.OrgID, key.UserID)
158			if !ok {
159				writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "the key's owner is no longer a member")
160				return
161			}
162			s.store.TouchAPIKey(key.ID, s.clock.Now())
163			p := auth.Principal{OrgID: key.OrgID, UserID: key.UserID, KeyID: key.ID, Role: m.Role}
164			if r.Method != http.MethodGet && !auth.CanWrite(p.Role) {
165				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "forbidden", "viewers can only read")
166				return
167			}
168			h(w, r, p)
169		}
170	}

145	func (s *Server) authed(h handler) http.HandlerFunc {
146		return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
147			token, ok := strings.CutPrefix(r.Header.Get("Authorization"), "Bearer ")
148			if !ok {
149				writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "send an API key as Authorization: Bearer <token>")
150				return
151			}
152			key, ok := s.store.APIKeyByToken(strings.TrimSpace(token))
153			if !ok || key.RevokedAt != nil {
154				writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "unknown or revoked API key")
155				return
156			}
157			m, ok := s.store.Member(key.OrgID, key.UserID)
158			if !ok {
159				writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "the key's owner is no longer a member")
160				return
161			}
162			s.store.TouchAPIKey(key.ID, s.clock.Now())
163			p := auth.Principal{OrgID: key.OrgID, UserID: key.UserID, KeyID: key.ID, Role: m.Role}
164			if r.Method != http.MethodGet && !auth.CanWrite(p.Role) {
165				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "forbidden", "viewers can only read")
166				return
167			}

169		}

The role table is enforced at every route, and the member, invite, key and last-owner rules are implemented under the store lock. One rule is wrong, though. The task says demoting the only owner is 409 `last_owner` "also when the owner does it to themselves." The self-change check in `updateMember` runs first and returns 403, so a sole owner demoting themselves gets 403, not 409. The test at `internal/api/roles_test.go` (the `TestRoleChangesRules` line with `e.Acme.Owner.ID` and `e.Acme.Key`) asserts that wrong 403, so the suite locks the bug in. Self-removal by the sole owner is correct, since `DELETE` skips the self check.

Findings:

1. **`internal/api/team.go:85-89` (`updateMember`)**: The self-change check returns 403 before the last-owner check. A sole owner `PATCH /v1/members/{own id}` with any role other than owner must return 409 `last_owner`. Fix: when `target == p.UserID`, let the request reach `SetMemberRoleIf` only for the last-owner case, or run the last-owner check first and return `ErrLastOwner` when the caller is the sole owner and the new role is not owner. Otherwise keep the 403. Then update the `expectForbidden` line in `TestRoleChangesRules` that targets `e.Acme.Owner.ID` with `e.Acme.Key` to expect 409 `last_owner`, and add a test that a non-sole owner demoting themselves still gets 403.
